items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He didn't know Ziggy from Harry from Chris Griffin.

ctx.x: How did he hold a band together? Was that someone else’s job really?

Well he chose the musicians he wanted. He had a manager of course, you know that man. I’ll tell you how foggy — now Sid Weiss, the bass player that worked with Benny Goodman on the old band, an old timer, he told me that in the old days, of course I really, Benny liked me and I had a bad temper in those days and I almost hit him actually. And I used to tell him — I can’t use that f word. But you foggy idiot. You know, a foggy idiot. Because he would do some of the dumbest things. And I was just a kid. You know I…

Auld, got everybody. And the most important thing is that Benny said to Joe Glaser, “Get me Ziggy Elman.” Now I came in with them to the rehearsal and Benny looks at Joe Glaser, looks around to him. He said, “I told you to get me Ziggy Elman.” He says, “That’s Ziggy.” “That’s not Ziggy Elman.” “What do you mean?” He walked away. He didn’t know Ziggy from Harry from Chris Griffin. He didn’t whose name was who. “Get me Ziggy Elman.” But when it came to playing the clarinet, that was probably some of the most…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: didn’t know the difference between Chris Griffin and Harry James.

ctx.x: You know everybody has a Benny Goodman story but not everybody living — one of my most fun times is I used to do a lot of the jazz cruises, you know, 90 musicians would be on a cruise. And Mel Powell was on one of the cruises. And Mel Powell worked with Benny Goodman way before I did. And we sat there one night talking about Benny Goodman stories, and who else? Maybe Ken Peplowski, he worked for Benny Goodman. Whoever was there that knew Benny Goodman, and it was actually like a bunch of comedians sitting around…

of them, the agent, he told Joe Glaser, “Get me” this is in New York, “Get me Ziggy Elman.” Ziggy Elman was in California. So I go to the first rehearsal I went with Joe Glaser to Benny’s rehearsal, even though I wasn’t going to be on the show I just wanted to hear the band. And I’m standing with Joe Glaser and Benny looks at me and he says, “I asked you to get me Ziggy Elman on the trumpet” he says. “That’s Ziggy Elman, I flew him in” and Joe Glaser would use every F word in the world, you know I’m telling you,…
